objectives: Keep the registers, books and case files through a whole year, from the first entry to the closing of the volumes.
Apply the retention periods and the rules for destroying or transferring records.
Prepare the office for an inspection by the Ministry of Justice.
Apply data protection rules to identity documents, identity numbers and the archive.

cards.front: What does the official archive contain?
cards.back: Registers and books, case files, other documents, and the **seal** (Art. 28(2) ЗННД).
Nobody without the notary's **consent**, except in the cases provided by law (Art. 21(1) ЗННД).

cards.front: A police officer asks to take a case file to the station. What does the office need?
cards.back: A **written order of a judge or prosecutor**; copies go against signature to the official named in it; originals leave only with the notary personally (Art. 28(3)–(4) ЗННД).
On **1 January** each year (Art. 5–6 and 10(4) Наредба № 32).

cards.front: How long are case files for deeds kept?
cards.back: **5 years**; files for wills and deposits, and decisions on circumstantial verifications, **100 years** (Art. 10(5) Наредба № 32).

cards.front: What happens to records after 100 years?
cards.back: They go to the **State Archives** for permanent storage (Art. 28а(3) ЗННД).
Only after **agreement with the State Archives** (Art. 28а(2) ЗННД).

cards.front: The notary dies. Who orders the sealing of the archive?
cards.back: The **president of the district court** (Art. 36(2) ЗННД); the heirs must ask for it at once, else the mayor or the district judge (Art. 22(2)–(3) Наредба № 32).
Inspectors of the **Ministry of Justice** with **inspector-notaries** (Art. 80б ЗННД).

cards.front: A clerk wants to photocopy a client's identity card "for the file". When is that allowed?
cards.back: Only when **a law provides** for it, for example AML due diligence (Art. 25г ЗЗЛД; Art. 53(1) ЗМИП). Otherwise the office records the data.

cards.front: Is free public access to identity numbers allowed?
cards.back: **No**, unless a law provides otherwise (Art. 25ж(1) ЗЗЛД).

cards.front: What is the deadline under the Regulation to notify a risky data breach?
cards.back: **72 hours** to the Commission for Personal Data Protection (Art. 33 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679).

quiz.question: A police officer asks to take a case file to the station. What does the office need?
options: A written order of a judge or prosecutor naming the official
The service card of the officer and a receipt for the file
The written consent of the client whose file it is
Nothing; the police have free access to every notarial file by law
quiz.explanation: Art. 28(3) ЗННД: files and documents leave the archive only on a written order of a judge or prosecutor; copies are handed against signature to the official named in the order. Art. 21: nobody has access to the archive without the notary's consent, except by law.

quiz.question: A graphology expert must examine an original signature in a deed. Where?
options: In the office, in the notary's presence
At the expert's laboratory, with a receipt
At the court, after the clerk brings it
Anywhere; a certified copy is enough for the expert
quiz.explanation: Art. 28(4) ЗННД: originals leave the office only on an express order under Art. 28(3) and only with the notary personally, and an expert examination is made only in the notary's presence. A copy does not serve for a signature examination.

quiz.question: The general register of 2014 is still in the office in 2026. What may the office do?
options: Destroy it after agreement with the State Archives
Throw it away; the 10-year period has expired
Hand it to the Registry Agency for permanent storage
Keep it; registers are kept for 100 years
quiz.explanation: Art. 28а(2) ЗННД: the general register and the books of item 6 and 7 are kept 10 years and are then destroyed after agreement with the State Archives. The alphabetical index, the register of wills and the books of acts and wills are kept 100 years (Art. 28а(3)).

quiz.question: How long does the office keep the book of notarial wills?
options: 100 years, then to the State Archives
10 years, then destroyed after agreement
5 years, as a case file for a deed
Forever, in the office of the notary
quiz.explanation: Art. 28а(3) ЗННД: the alphabetical index, the register of deposited wills and the books of acts subject to entry and of wills are kept 100 years and then handed to the State Archives for permanent storage.

quiz.question: The notary dies. What happens first to the archive?
options: It is sealed by order of the president of the district court
The heirs take it to the family home for safekeeping
The clerk continues to work with it until a new notary comes
It is sent to the Ministry of Justice by courier
quiz.explanation: Art. 36(2) ЗННД and Art. 22(1) of Ordinance No. 32: the archive is sealed by order of the president of the district court, with a protocol and an inventory. The heirs must ask for the sealing at once (Art. 22(2)–(3)); the president may also order it ex officio (Art. 22(4)).

quiz.question: Who receives the archive of a notary who left the profession?
options: Another notary of the district who wants it, else the registration judge
The Notary Chamber, which keeps it in its own archive
The State Archives, as the place of permanent storage of every notarial record
The heirs of the notary, as the owners of the office
quiz.explanation: Art. 23(2) of Ordinance No. 32: at the unsealing a representative of the Chamber makes an inventory, and the archive goes to another notary of the same district who wants it, or to the registration judge; Art. 23(3): the Council of Notaries decides when the heirs name no notary.

quiz.question: A client asks for a signature certification. May the clerk photocopy the client's ID card "for the file"?
options: Only when a law provides for it, such as AML due diligence
Yes, always; the copy proves the identity check in every case file
No, never; identity documents are never copied
Only with the oral consent of the client
quiz.explanation: Art. 25г ЗЗЛД: a controller may copy an identity document only when a law provides for it; Art. 53(1) ЗМИП provides it for due diligence. For a certification without due diligence the office records the data of the document in the endorsement and the register.

quiz.question: A clerk wants to e-mail a list of clients with their identity numbers to a supplier. Is it allowed?
options: No; identity numbers are not disclosed freely, and secrecy applies
Yes, if the supplier signs a confidentiality contract with the office first
Yes, if the supplier is a trusted partner of the office
Yes, for marketing to the existing clients of the office
quiz.explanation: Art. 25ж(1) ЗЗЛД: free access to information with identity numbers is not allowed unless a law provides otherwise; Art. 49 and 26 ЗННД bind the employees to secrecy about the clients. A contract with a supplier does not create a legal ground.

quiz.question: What do inspectors check in the registers?
options: Continuity, daily closing with signature and seal, no unauthorised corrections
The colours of the covers and the numbering of the pages
The private bank accounts of the notary and the salaries of the staff of the office
Only the number of acts for the year in each of the registers
quiz.explanation: Art. 5 of Ordinance No. 32 sets how the registers are kept: continuous numbering, every day's entries closed with the notary's signature and seal, corrections made only in the prescribed way. The inspection under Art. 80б ЗННД verifies these rules.

quiz.question: An office laptop with scanned identity documents is stolen. What should happen?
options: Inform the notary at once; notify the authority within 72 hours if needed
Nothing; the laptop was locked with a password
Buy a new laptop and restore the scanned files from the backup of the office server
Inform the clients at the next visit of each of them
quiz.explanation: Art. 33 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679: the controller notifies the supervisory authority of a personal data breach within 72 hours, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk; Art. 34: persons at high risk are informed. The notary, as controller, assesses the risk and decides.

quiz.question: A case file for a notarial will made in 2019 is in the archive. May the office destroy it in 2026?
options: No; case files for wills are kept 100 years
Yes; case files are kept 5 years
Yes, after agreement with the State Archives
No; wills are kept until the testator dies
quiz.explanation: Art. 10(5) of Ordinance No. 32: case files for deeds and circumstantial verifications are kept five years and then destroyed after agreement with the State Archives; case files for wills and deposits, and the decisions on circumstantial verifications, are kept one hundred years and then handed to the State Archives.

quiz.question: An heir asks to see the data of the deceased client in the case file. What does the office do?
options: Gives access to the heir, who has a legal interest
Refuses; the data of a dead person are not protected
Refuses; only a court may order such access
Gives access to anyone who asks about a dead person
quiz.explanation: Art. 25е(2) ЗЗЛД: the controller gives the heirs, and other persons with a legal interest, access to the personal data of a deceased person, including a copy, within the terms of the Regulation; Art. 28а(4) ЗННД: inquiries in case files are given only to the parties, their successors and their representatives.
